jurisdiction.drafting: AI organizes and drafts. People decide. The Legislative Reference Bureau drafts the final bill text for any legislator who introduces it.

jurisdiction.generalFundTradeoff: the general fund, where it competes with schools, health care, housing, and everything else the state pays for
jurisdiction.handoffText: The package goes to the offices of the state representative and state senator for this district. They decide whether to introduce it. The public record stays open either way.
jurisdiction.timing: The 2027 session opens January 20. Bills are introduced in the first week or two, so packages should reach legislators by early January.

issue.name: Invasive species
issue.title: Invasive species in Hawaiʻi
facts: Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, renamed from the Department of Agriculture by Act 236 (2025).
The department and governor can now declare a biosecurity emergency to stop a pest from spreading.
A new deputy for biosecurity takes charge of inspections and pest control programs.
$8.5 million over two years for the Hawaiʻi Invasive Species Council, plus $500,000 each for the Hawaiʻi Ant Lab and the coconut rhinoceros beetle response.
lists: House Committee on Agriculture & Food Systems
Senate Committee on Agriculture and Environment
Money bills also pass through House Finance and Senate Ways and Means
groups: Leans toward protecting farms and keeping costs off residents. Skeptical of visitor fees and higher fines.
Leans toward stronger enforcement and new funding sources, including visitors.

statements.text: Every island should have a rapid-response crew that can treat a new little fire ant find within 72 hours.
Plants and soil shipped between islands should be inspected the same way as shipments from the mainland.
The state should publish a public map of confirmed pest sightings, updated weekly.
Fines for knowingly moving infested material should go up.
Funding for invasive species should come from a dedicated source, not compete with the general budget every year.
Homeowners should get free little fire ant treatment kits and training.
Visitors should pay a fee that goes directly to biosecurity.
Farmers who report a new pest quickly should be protected from losing their whole crop without compensation.
Schools should teach keiki to recognize the worst invasive pests.

costOptions.name: Rapid-response crews
costOptions.impact: {n} crews of 4 staff with gear, so each major island can respond within 72 hours.
costOptions.basis: About $73,000 per biosecurity position, based on the 2024 law that funded 44 positions for $3.2 million, plus equipment.
costOptions.billText: establish {n} rapid response teams, assigned so that every island can begin treatment of a newly detected little fire ant infestation within seventy-two hours of confirmation

costOptions.name: Interisland plant and soil inspections
costOptions.impact: {n} inspectors at interisland ports and cargo hubs.
costOptions.billText: inspect plants and soil shipped between islands to the same standard as shipments from outside the State, with {n} additional inspector positions

costOptions.name: Public pest sighting map
costOptions.impact: Weekly public map built on the pest dashboard Act 236 already requires.
costOptions.billText: publish a public map of confirmed pest detections, updated at least weekly, as part of the pest dashboard required by Act 236, Session Laws of Hawaii 2025

costOptions.name: Study a dedicated funding source
costOptions.impact: One-time study with recommendations to the legislature.
costOptions.billText: study and recommend a dedicated, recurring funding source for biosecurity programs and report its findings to the legislature

costOptions.name: Free fire ant kits for homeowners
costOptions.impact: {n} households a year get bait and training.
costOptions.basis: About $40 per household for bait and training, estimated.
costOptions.billText: provide free little fire ant treatment supplies and training to up to {n} residential households each year

costOptions.name: Farmer compensation fund
costOptions.impact: {total} a year to cover crop losses from required pest control.
costOptions.basis: Set by the legislature; no standard cost.
costOptions.billText: establish a compensation fund of {dollars} each year for farmers who promptly report a new pest and suffer crop losses from required control measures

costOptions.name: Pest lessons in schools
costOptions.impact: Lesson materials and teacher training statewide.
costOptions.billText: work with the department of education to offer invasive pest identification lessons in public schools

revenue.name: Visitor biosecurity fee
revenue.note: Per visitor, based on about 9.64 million visitor arrivals in 2025. Paid by visitors, not residents.
revenue.billText: There is established a biosecurity visitor fee of {fee} per visitor arrival, to be deposited into a special fund for the purposes of this Act.

revenue.name: Raise fines for moving infested material
revenue.note: Penalties mainly deter. The revenue estimate is rough.
revenue.billText: The penalties for knowingly transporting material infested with a restricted pest shall be increased.
